title: k8s-node-provisioning-debug-scratchpad
body:
Context / symptom:
- Intermittent failures during node provisioning for new AWS spot instances in cluster-prod-us-west-2. New nodes enter NotReady or stay in NotReady state after kubelet comes up (seen ~6/20 attempts). Some nodes never register with control plane.

What I observed (timeline):
1) kubeadm join completes successfully on instance, prints join token accepted, but node never shows in `kubectl get nodes`.
2) On other attempts, node registers but remains NotReady with `KubeletNotReady` and frequent `ImagePullBackOff` on infra pods.
3) Sometimes pods are stuck in ContainerCreating with message: "failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up sandbox container"

Commands I ran and outputs (snippets):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
  NAME           STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
  ip-10-0-12-34  NotReady   <none>   10m   v1.25.3

- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-12-34
  Taints:             <none>
  Conditions:
    Type              Status  LastHeartbeatTime
    Ready             False   2026-02-28T14:03:21Z  -> KubeletNotReady: container runtime not ready

- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager  <-- key excerpts
  Feb 28 13:58:12 ip-10-0-12-34 kubelet[2311]: E0228 13:58:12.345678    2311 kubelet.go:2345] Container runtime status unknown: failed to connect to containerd socket: dial unix /run/containerd/containerd.sock: connect: no such file or directory
  Feb 28 13:58:13 ip-10-0-12-34 systemd[1]: Started kubelet: The Kubernetes Node Agent.

- sudo systemctl status containerd
  ● containerd.service - containerd
     Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/containerd.service; enabled)
     Active: failed (Result: exit-code) since Sat 2026-02-28 13:57:50 UTC; 12s ago
  Feb 28 13:57:50 containerd[1987]: time="2026-02-28T13:57:50.123Z" level=error msg="failed to start listener: listen unix /run/containerd/containerd.sock: permission denied"

- docker/ctr not running; attempted restart: sudo systemctl restart containerd -> failed with same permission error

- kubeadm join logs on instance: "[discovery] Created cluster-info discovery client, requesting with bootstrap token" then "[preflight] Running pre-flight checks" -> no obvious cluster-side denial.

- helm upgrade --install infra-stack ./charts/infra -n infra --wait
  Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: cannot re-use a name that is still in use
  (this was on a different node attempt where chart release partially installed, likely due to timeout)

Hypotheses / root cause suspects:
- containerd failing to create unix socket due to permission/SELinux or leftover /run dir owner mismatch after AMI bootstrap (cloud-init step might chown /run incorrectly).
- race between cloud-init finalization and container runtime startup leading to socket file permissions owned by root:root but kubelet/containerd run as different user on our AMI.
- spot instance bootstrapping with our startup script sometimes failing during `apt-get` -> partial install of containerd -> service fails.
- kubelet complaining shows container runtime not ready which explains NotReady and ContainerCreating timeouts.
- For the nodes that register but show ImagePullBackOff: maybe network/CNI not initialised because kube-proxy or CNI DaemonSet stuck pending until container runtime healthy.

Things tried (and results):
- sudo chown root:root /run/containerd - no effect; containerd still logs permission denied on socket creation.
- strace containerd (quick check) shows EACCES when creating socket bind at /run/containerd/containerd.sock -> seems like an SELinux/AppArmor or mount namespace issue.
- checked dmesg for SELinux AVC denies -> nothing obvious; our AMI doesn't run SELinux enabled by default but some hosts have apparmor enabled.
- switched AMI to a known-good baseline (ami-0abcd1234) for one test node -> containerd started cleanly and node joined. That suggests AMI drift is plausible.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Add a boot-time sleep 30s in our cloud-init before starting kubelet/containerd to give package installs time to finish: reduced failures in a small sample but not eliminated.
- Fallback to on-demand (non-spot) for provisioning in that ASG to reduce noise while debugging.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Reproduce consistently with a small fleet using the problematic AMI; capture full /var/log/boot.log, cloud-init-output.log, and containerd journal.
- Add verbose containerd debug logs (set log-level debug) on a repro node and collect /run and mount output right after boot.
- Inspect cloud-init scripts: check any chown/chmod on /run or sockets. Audit for racey operations that might change /run ownership.
- Try disabling AppArmor on repro AMI to rule out LSM interference.
- Update bootstrap to ensure container runtime package installation is fully complete before enabling/starting the service (use systemd units with proper Wants/After or cloud-init runcmd ordering).
- Create a short test that runs `stat -c "%U:%G %a" /run /run/containerd` and `ls -lZ /run/containerd` during bootstrap to capture ownership + selinux label.
- File follow-up: JIRA K8S-345 with logs + repro steps. Assign to Platform Eng and tag infra team.

Notes to self:
- When grabbing logs, include `journalctl -u containerd -b -1` (previous boot) because failure often happens in first boot phase.
- If AMI drift is confirmed, build a new AMI pipeline step that verifies container runtime start, otherwise fail the AMI.

Unresolved questions:
- Why does containerd report permission denied on a socket path under /run even when /run is root-owned? Is there an unexpected mount/overlay or namespace where socket creation is blocked?
- Are there differences in systemd unit files across AMIs (containerd packaged versions) that change the runtime user?
- Could cloud-init be creating /run/containerd as a tmpfs with wrong mode?

Logs & artifacts collected (what I'll attach to the JIRA):
- /var/log/cloud-init-output.log (2 nodes)
- journalctl -u containerd and kubelet (full)
- `ls -laZ /run` and `stat` outputs captured at boot
- kubeadm join output and kubelet preflight logs
- helm release partial install logs for the infra chart (timing info)

If anyone else is digging into this, start with the containerd journal around boot and the cloud-init-output.log. Tagging Jordan/ Alex since they helped repro earlier.

-- emily
